original.target_description: Relationship between the Gender Empowerment Measure and men's emphasis on a mate's physical attractiveness (ranking data). Correlation across cultures in Buss et al. (1990).

n.exclusions: Two cultures lacked ranking data; index-specific available cultures are given in table column headers. Differing subsamples of the same broader culture share index values.

replication.target_description: physical attractiveness; ranking task; GII; participant-sex × gender-equality interaction from linear mixed model controlling for Galton’s problem, with country and geographic-region effects, age/sex predictors; 2986 participants from 36 countries. The supplied description names GEM, but replication Table 1 uses GII, explicitly chosen for similarity to GEM; these are different indices. The supplied target is a men-only association. Replication Table 1 instead reports a participant-sex × gender-equality interaction in both sexes, not a men-only slope. Extracted values describe the located table test and must not be treated as the men-only test.

n.sample_role: participants in ranking-task analytic sample, clustered in 36 countries; both sexes
n.exclusions: Age missing or outside 16–60 (927), not exclusively heterosexual (1212); rating task additionally excludes 35 participants lacking all three trait ratings; only countries with more than 9 participants analyzed. Printed task-specific analytic n retained without deriving counts.

notes: Original title and replication title verified in full texts. Original p values are significance-footnote bounds; unmarked cells have no numerical p printed. Replication source is the original OSF DOCX primary file (culture_sex_differences.docx; OSF file 5c0671029de61900191a5397), parsed read-only into the shared text cache. Exact table/row locations are used because DOCX has no reliable printed page numbering. GDI is the replication paper’s Gender Development Index, selected by its authors for similarity to the older Gender-Related Development Index. The supplied description names GEM, but replication Table 1 uses GII, explicitly chosen for similarity to GEM; these are different indices. The supplied target is a men-only association. Replication Table 1 instead reports a participant-sex × gender-equality interaction in both sexes, not a men-only slope. Extracted values describe the located table test and must not be treated as the men-only test. No authors’ narrative verdict for the specific men-only association was located; narrative success left null. Replication estimates are printed model coefficients; gender-equality variables were standardized by the authors. Methods reports the task-specific analytic samples used here despite different abstract/initial-sample totals.
